scope: Independent read-only functional preservation, escaped data identity, accessibility semantics and exact191/192 coverage review. No product, ledger, backend or old evidence edits; no tests executed by this reviewer.
functional_preservation: Personally reconstructed all nine declared literal edits from genuine before bytes and verified exact current module. Changes are visible identity/consequence text and accessible names; no request, ownership, refresh, busy, selection, scheduling, persistence or export expression changes.

Inspected current getRecycleBin, restoreRecycleBatch and purgeRecycleBatch transport: list GET, encoded immutable batch id POST with {}, DELETE with {confirm:true}. Staged proof lists four identical AST calls and zero full-project TypeScript diagnostics.

Read backend router and restore/list service only. Existing require_admin router dependency, UUID paths, explicit purge confirmation, per-item restoration and already-restored/unknown errors remain server responsibilities. Browser fixtures do not verify authorization or actual database writes.

Applied recovery script retains 29 original assertions, covers full/partial/zero responses, one mutation despite synthetic duplicate clicks, initial retry, confirmed-outcome read-back failures with GET-only retry, detached mutation/read completion and deliberate external focus ownership. Read report contains48 passed cases across three engines and320/1280; context report contains12 passed engine/width/theme cases.
security_and_accessibility: New batch id and action name HTML interpolate through esc; outcome, conflict labels/reasons and optional actor metadata escape on render. Confirmation is native text. Immutable dataset id remains original request key, CSS.escape scopes outcome targeting.

Context fixtures assert script-like member/actor strings remain literal and emit no script/b elements; equal-count batches have distinct complete visible ids and distinct action accessible names. Optional absent actors and malformed/no-zone timestamps have explicit readable fallbacks.

Personally viewed actual context-320-dark.png: complete long identities wrap inside cards, absent-account/time messages remain readable and buttons stay separated. This screenshot contains metadata contexts, not restore conflicts.

Native buttons retain Enter/pointer activation, disabled busy state, visible irreversible wording and status feedback. Focus restoration is guarded against intentional outside movement. No native screen reader, physical device, computed contrast or native browser zoom certification follows from these checks.

exact_condition_assessments.requirement: Refine recycle-bin cards and tables so record type, deletion context, restore scope and conflicts are immediately understandable.

conditions.condition: Recycle cards and tables identify record type, deletion context and the exact restore scope.
conditions.assessment: supported for implemented recycle cards; no separate recycle table rendering exists
conditions.evidence: Current cards include kind/count, full deletion batch id, deleted time/actor or fallback, expiry/restored metadata, labels and explicit batch-only restore scope. Context fixture includes all four supported kinds and equal-count distinct batches.

conditions.condition: Restore conflicts and unavailable optional metadata remain understandable in narrow layouts and both themes.
conditions.evidence: Optional metadata narrow/both-theme context assertions and actual screenshots pass; partial/zero conflict text is asserted in48 recovery cases with width320/1280, but recovery fixture does not explicitly exercise both themes or capture conflict screenshots.

exact_condition_assessments.acceptance_recommendation: Keep open until narrow conflict state is captured and checked in both themes, as required by evidence_needed.

exact_condition_assessments.requirement: Verify restore and permanent-delete controls independently, keeping their consequences and supported backend capabilities clearly separated.

conditions.condition: Restore returns the supported record to the expected location and explains conflicts without implying permanent deletion.
conditions.assessment: frontend response handling supported; end-to-end expected location unproven
conditions.evidence: Fixture response and refreshed recycle list are asserted, including conflict labels and reasons. No disposable database mutation plus operational destination read-back is present in these reports. Historical candidates inspected are explicitly fully mocked too.

conditions.condition: Permanent delete separately names its irreversible consequence; cancellation causes no request, and unsupported capabilities are explained rather than simulated.
conditions.assessment: irreversible wording and cancellation supported; refusal coverage incomplete
conditions.evidence: Native confirmation specifies selected batch and cannot-be-undone; dismissal emits no mutation in twelve context cases and six purge recovery cases. Current scenarios do not independently exercise mutation404/409/422 refusal or unsupported capabilities.

exact_condition_assessments.acceptance_recommendation: Keep open. Supply authorized disposable-fixture destination read-back and separate refusal/unsupported-capability checks; do not replace with mocked success counts.

nonblocking_existing_risks: Numeric batch.count/result values are trusted under existing typed server schema; no runtime schema validation was introduced. Existing count interpolation is not covered by malformed-type adversarial fixtures.

Intro says restore puts records back as they were, qualified by new visible per-batch conflict warning. Partial batches retain original total count; server actually attempts only pending records. This review does not claim that repeated partial response accounting is exhaustively covered.
Fixture id values are deliberately readable strings although genuine server batch ids are UUIDs; transport-contract byte assertions are frontend checks, not server validation tests.
blockers: 191 lacks explicit narrow conflict screenshots and both-theme conflict checks.
192 lacks disposable persisted restoration destination read-back and independent backend refusal/unsupported capability evidence.
recommendation: No product regression found in nine presentation edits. Do not grant exact191/192 acceptance from current evidence alone.
